correctness.rationale: The proof was reconstructed from the frozen package rather than accepted from its prior review. Under the exponential order-statistic representation, the exceedances above the kth exponential threshold are independent Exp(1), and the exact Hall increment is \(Y+\alpha\ell_z(Y)\). Integrating against Exp(1) gives \(m(z)=-\beta z/(1+\beta)+\beta z^2/(1+2\beta)+O(z^3)\). Since \(A=-\beta z\), the oracle correction cancels the linear term and leaves the positive quadratic term for either sign of \(c\). The chosen threshold window has \(r_n/\delta_n\to\infty\) and \(|z_n|r_n=o(\delta_n)\); order-statistic concentration is therefore superexponentially negligible on the \(k\delta_n^2\) scale. Centered Hall corrections are uniformly \(O(|z_n|)\), so Hoeffding likewise makes their \(\varepsilon\delta_n\) deviations negligible. What remains is the lower moderate deviation of a Gamma(k-1,1) average, whose rate is \(k\delta_n^2/2\). The missing 1/k mean term is negligible because \(k\delta_n^2\to\infty\).
risks: The theorem is exact-Hall and oracle-only; a third-order tail term can modify the quadratic residual coefficient.

final_claim: For the exact eventual Hall quantile \(U(t)=t^{1/\alpha}(1+c t^{-\beta})\), the oracle first-order bias-corrected Hill statistic has residual normalized bias \(\alpha A(n/k)^2/[\beta(1+2\beta)]\); when \(\delta_n=\theta_n+\alpha A(n/k)^2/[\beta(1+2\beta)]\to0\) and \(k\delta_n^2\to\infty\), the one-sided conservative error probability has logarithmic asymptotic \(-\log P\{(1-\theta_n)/\widetilde H_{k,n}>\alpha\}\sim k\delta_n^2/2\), including the zero-rescaling \(kA(n/k)^4\) regime and the stated target-decay \(k\)-scale.
limitations: Exact eventual Hall quantile only; oracle correction; one-sided asymptotic statement; no finite-sample guarantee.
